prompt:
An investigation is performed to verify Ohm's law (V = I * R) for a metallic conductor.
The potential difference V across the conductor is measured with a voltmeter as the current I is varied using a variable resistor.
The student plots a graph of V on the vertical axis against I on the horizontal axis.
[FIGURE PLACEHOLDER: Graph of potential difference V on the vertical axis against current I on the horizontal axis. The plotted points lie along a straight line of positive gradient. The line of best fit intersects the vertical axis at V = +0.40 V when I = 0.0 A. At I = 0.50 A, the line passes through V = 2.90 V.]
(a) State the type of experimental error indicated by the fact that the line of best fit does not pass through the origin. [1]
(b) Assuming the ammeter has no zero error, determine the zero error of the voltmeter, including its sign. [1]
(c) Calculate the resistance R of the conductor from the gradient of the graph, showing your working clearly. [2]
(d) Explain whether taking twenty additional sets of readings with the same voltmeter and ammeter and replotting the line of best fit will remove the vertical intercept. [1]
(e) State what practical action the student should take to ensure future measurements with this voltmeter pass through the origin. [1]

parts.description: Identify error type from non-zero intercept
Explain effect of additional readings on intercept
State practical remedy for zero error

part_enrichment.guidance: Recognize that a persistent non-zero intercept indicates a systematic error (zero error).
At I = 0, the voltmeter reads +0.40 V, which is the zero error.
State that repeated measurements cannot remove a systematic error.
Adjust the mechanical/electrical zero or subtract +0.40 V from all readings.

mark_scheme.criterion: Part (d): No, because repeated measurements and averaging cannot eliminate a systematic error, so the intercept will remain +0.40 V.
Part (e): Adjust the zero-adjust screw / zero button on the voltmeter (or subtract +0.40 V from all recorded readings).

hints: In part (a), an intercept where there should be none is a hallmark of systematic error.
In part (b), what does the voltmeter read when current is zero?
In part (c), calculate gradient using a large triangle from the graph coordinates given.
solution: (a) Systematic error (zero error). (b) +0.40 V. (c) Gradient = (2.90 - 0.40) / (0.50 - 0.00) = 2.50 / 0.50 = 5.0 ohms. (d) No, repeating measurements cannot remove a systematic error. (e) Adjust the mechanical zero screw on the meter or subtract 0.40 V from all voltage readings.
teacher_walkthrough: (a) When I = 0, V should be 0. An intercept of +0.40 V indicates a systematic zero error in the voltmeter.
(b) Since I = 0 corresponds to V = +0.40 V, the zero error is +0.40 V.
(c) The equation of the line is V = I * R + 0.40. The gradient is R = Delta_V / Delta_I = (2.90 - 0.40) / (0.50 - 0.00) = 2.50 / 0.50 = 5.0 ohms.
(d) Taking more readings with the same meter will not remove the intercept because every single reading contains the exact same +0.40 V systematic offset.
(e) To eliminate the error: adjust the meter's zero screw before measuring, or subtract +0.40 V from each reading during data processing.

provenance.independence_statement: Authored 6-mark structured problem connecting V-I graph intercept and gradient to zero error and resistance.
